questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That there would be opportunities to speak the language im studying, as well as the city/country being somewhere i've never been before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of assistance from the international office at my host uni - they were really extremely kind and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were kitchens in the doorm, as well as cafeterias at the uni + one at the dorm. There were no cooking utensils in the doorm kitchens tho, you had to buy everything, which felt a bit wasteful, since I werent able to bring the things back home to my own country.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Bring a pillow + kitchen utensils, unless you are okay with buying that stuff on site. (If you live in the dorm-rooms).

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been nice to know how many things we had to bring ourselves (kitchen utensils, pillow, duvet etc).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember, but I think it was alright (though quite a lot of paperwork and different locations that those had to be done at.) The International office was very helpful!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office had students help us manage and help with potential language barriers.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the classes that looked like they would be offered (on the KIMEP website) weren't on the registration list, but I was happy with what I ended up with and I believe we were able to register courses before a lot of other students, meaning it was easier to get exactly what we wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have different options for classes ready, so that if something isnt offered, you have other options available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general it was very good, but it would be nice if the KIMEP website and the programme plan were aligned. So fx, if it says a course will be offered in the fall semester on the website, it should also be offered on registration, otherwise it shouldnt say it would be offered on the KIMEP website.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 1 class that were a mix of BA and MA. I really liked it though!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different! At my home uni its more of "here is the theory"/"here is what people in the field have done before" and then we have to use that information and apply it ourselves as well as a big focus on critical thinking, whereas KIMEP was more about learning things by heart/memorizing information. I was a bit disappointed in the intense use of AI at KIMEP uni. Some professors didn't use it, which was nice, but even if the professor didn't, almost all the students did, which made the presentations part of the year (towards the end, where we had to do presentations in almost all courses) really boring, cause it was so painfully obvious that 90% of all the presentations were made by AI.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Russian Speaking Practise, Intensive Russian, Kazakh Spirituality, Petropolitics, Emerging Powers

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Petropolitics! It was very interesting, and the teacher was my absolute favourite. He can go off on a tangent, but his stories are always very interesting and he is quite a funny (and very clever!!) man. I learned so much about oil, tax-systems and international politics in this course!
All my russian-language courses were also really good!

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Translitteration of passport from danish/english into russian. Kitchen utensils, duvet, pillow when moving in. Fitness membership.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was way cheaper than I thought. Eating out was also quite cheap, even on a tight budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! And they send out e-mails as well as inform you in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe a club! I didn't do that, but I used the free gym on campus, that all uni-students are welcome to use.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nature! (Hiking, horseback riding, skiing, ice skating, renting a car and driving further to see things like petroglyphs, the Great Steppe, lakes, Charyn Canyon etc). On national holidays there might be festivals or music playing, and KIMEP was located next to a big square that offen had concerts or events happening.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Alright! People are very nice and offen times interested in you if you are from a country far away. Not everyone speaks english, but people are still very nice and don't mind the language barrier too much.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be a bit difficult, but try to just speak with people in your class or join clubs/sport teams while you are there!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably the bathroom/toilets and not being able to throw toiletpaper in the toilet. Other than that it was fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people and how nice (most) people were. Also the architecture of the city as well as all the delicious food the city had to offer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for A LOT of AI use, and try to not fall into the trap of using it too much yourself. Be prepared for a lot of homework in your russian language classes! Remember to plan some of your weekends for longer travel (other cities or near-by countries) or/and events, since its easy to be tired and just stay in the part of the city that you already know.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing a new part of the world and meeting new people. I would recommend EVERYONE to try to visit Almaty/KZ (or generally Central Asia).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably getting my phone registered, but that was also a new thing, so the system around the registration were developing and changing. The international office were very helpful during this very long process tho!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
